subject.title: [Feature]: Make Skill Workshop extensible for custom skill creation workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a core/plugin SDK skill-creation authority that can route custom workflows before `skill_workshop`, or keep Skill Workshop as the direct governed path and rely on existing skills, plugin tools, and tool policy?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent boundary affects product UX, plugin API shape, config/policy semantics, and the single Skill Workshop write boundary, so model judgment should not choose it alone.

options.title: Design a narrow authority hook
options.body: Add a small plugin/skill authority surface that can prepare validated proposal content before final Skill Workshop persistence, with docs and compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep current routing model
options.body: Document that custom workflows should use skills/plugin tools plus tool policy, and close this direction if maintainers do not want a new authority concept.

options.title: Limit to ClawHub convention
options.body: Treat custom skill creators as ClawHub-distributed bundles/plugins without a core routing guarantee, and revisit only if a concrete missing API remains.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authority hook
recommendation.body: Add a small plugin/skill authority surface that can prepare validated proposal content before final Skill Workshop persistence, with docs and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest feature-history trail for the Skill Workshop proposal lifecycle and would be best placed to judge whether a new authority hook fits that boundary.
